<!--
Plain-markdown template so agents can fill it via `gh issue create --body`.
Humans: the form-based template is friendlier, use that one instead.

Every field below is required. An issue missing the quote or the fetched URL
will be closed without review — not out of hostility, but because an
unverifiable number costs more to check than to ignore.
-->

## Proposed change

**Platform:** <!-- e.g. bluesky -->
**Asset:** <!-- e.g. banner — use the id from data/sizes.json if it exists -->
**Change type:** <!-- correction | addition | source-moved | lost-its-source -->

**Current value:** <!-- what data/sizes.json says now, or "new entry" -->
**Proposed value:** <!-- what it should say -->

## Evidence

**URL fetched:** <!-- the exact URL you retrieved, not a search result -->
**Date fetched:** <!-- YYYY-MM-DD -->
**How:** <!-- plain fetch | headless browser | other. Say if the host bot-blocks. -->

**Quoted line from that page:**

```
Paste the sentence that states the number, verbatim. If you cannot quote it,
you did not verify it — propose published: false instead.
```

## Proposed JSON

<!--
The entry as it should appear in data/sizes.json. Omit fields you don't know
rather than guessing them. See data/schema.json for the shape.
-->

```json
{
  "id": "",
  "label": "",
  "render": "",
  "width": null,
  "height": null,
  "published": true,
  "source_url": "",
  "verified": ""
}
```

## Confirmations

- [ ] I read the number on the linked page. I did not infer it from another size guide, a blog post, or prior knowledge.
- [ ] The page I fetched is actually about this asset on this platform.
- [ ] If the platform publishes no such size, I set `published: false` and left `source_url` empty rather than filling it from memory.
- [ ] This issue was generated by an automated agent.

## Anything you could not verify

<!--
Say so plainly. "Couldn't confirm the file size cap, the page no longer
mentions it" is a useful issue. Silently omitting it is not.
-->
